conclusion: Both threads left in HardyRamanujantheorem.lean by run 43d363c1 are closed with zero sorrys and the standard three axioms: omega is bridged to ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors by rfl and the density theorem is restated so that every name in it is Mathlib's, and the pointwise log log n form is proved from the density form by splitting (0,N] at the square root of N. No existing statement, constant or proof was weakened or edited; the pointwise form consumes the variance bound (275) and the Mertens band (16) exactly as they stand.
confidence: Lean-arm confidence on the mathematics: the kernel accepted it, grep confirms zero sorrys, and #print axioms on all five new public statements returns only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Someone can lean on it as far as they lean on the Hardy-Ramanujan theorem that was already there, because nothing underneath it changed. Two caveats worth naming rather than burying. First, the bridge is a rfl between two library definitions that are spelled differently (n.primeFactors.card here, n.primeFactorsList.dedup.length in Mathlib); it is true today and would break if either definition were restated, which is exactly why it is now pinned by a theorem instead of assumed by a docstring. Second, the pointwise statement is the literal standard one, so the finitely many n below e^e (where log log n is negative and the condition is vacuously met) are inside the exceptional set; that is the classical statement's own convention and it costs nothing in density, but a reader comparing statement shapes should see it stated rather than discover it.

core_candidates.what: A preflight that checks for the Lean toolchain itself rather than reading a piped exit status

notes_for_operator: Case-log entry taken as Hunt #45 as assigned; #43, #44 and #45 were all free, so no renumbering was needed. One thing the brief could not know and that a reader of a green build should: 'lake build' over the whole ZetaLean package does not currently succeed in this container. ZetaLean.Pub1.CertL2 and ZetaLean.Pub1.CertAtoms log failures. They are outside this hunt's scope, and neither imports anything from ZetaLean.HardyRamanujan (checked by grep over their import closure), so neither can be a consequence of this run's edit. What I did not establish is why they fail: the two modules are expensive (one carries maxHeartbeats 4000000) and re-running them to capture the error was not a good use of the remaining budget, so it is possible this is a container resource limit rather than a source defect. The targeted build of the edited module and its full dependency chain is green; the whole-package build is not. Whether that is a live regression on main or a known state is an allocation question, so it is named here rather than acted on. Budget: the run finished inside 70 minutes, but roughly the first third of it went to installing a toolchain the environment was expected to have, which is the Core candidate above.
